The haves had something called PAL and coincidentally made all the cool games and demos. The Have-nots relied on bullshit NTSC which was pretty much limited to educational games and the occasional virus-laden boot loader.

Ram Air Reservoir Water Rake Cooler?

I didn't like the more or less stagnant air in my reservoir, while the system also seems to trap heat.

I have seen people using your standard 5" muffin fans, mounting a series of them on the lid. I don't like that for a few reasons. Like proximity to the nutrient solution, the fact that it leaves it wide open to light, and other debris which could be ruinous of the internal mechanics that the system depends on.

The scoops are formed form a gallon bottle of distilled water sliced in half with the ends taken off. The source of air movement for the tent is a Hurricane floor fan aimed directly at them from just a few feet in front of it, so they will always have a powerful feed.

Each scoop has six holes, each hole has a ~5" tube, of I believe 3/8" I.D. I can feel the air flowing through them. Whether or not it acts to cool the res I can't yet say. But it will certainly exchange the air in it at a better rate than without it. The tubes serve a few functions, including helping the air impinge on the water surface where the water falls are driving O2 down into the solution. They also block most debris that may find their way into those scoops. In particular any spilled Hydroton. They also won't let much light through, though that can be improved on using black tubing instead of clear. Finally, and of primacy concern, the sound from it didn't get too much worse.

So far I'm going with "probably worth it", and probably inadequate cooling. But it's "free", and meets my objectives .
